text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: PD-Auth-TokenFailure — auth-service: JWT verification errors spike > 8% (5m rolling). Affected: frontend-auth, api-gateway. Escalation level: L1 -> on-call.

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident PD-Auth-TokenFailure created and pages sent to primary on-call.

Alex G.: acked on PagerDuty, jumping in. seeing 502s at edge when requests require signed token validation. logs show 'JWT verification failed: kid mismatch' and `couldn't find key for kid \"e7a2f\"`.

Maria R.: I'm routing traffic to fallback auth-verifier (v1) via routing rule while Alex digs in. We should announce potential customer impact.

Jonah L.: Confirming: our JWKS cache returns old keys? curl to https://auth.redwood.example/.well-known/jwks.json shows two keys, latest kid `f3c9d` but tokens have `e7a2f`. Looks like signing service rotated keys but didn't push tokens/key metadata consistently.

Alex G.: repro: pasted token into local verifier, get `SignatureInvalid` and header shows `kid: e7a2f`. Signing-service logs at ~10:12Z: `rotated signing key, set active_kid=f3c9d` but didn't update key-publisher. Possible race during key rotation.

Priya S.: tagging @oncall-rotation-bot for handoff if this goes beyond 30m. Also starting a quick mitigation plan: 1) revert signing-service to previous key; 2) refresh JWKS publisher; 3) reload verifier caches. Which is fastest?

Alex G.: quick test: forcing auth-service to re-fetch JWKS (POST /admin/refresh-jwks) immediately reduces error rate from 8% -> 1.2% in Canary. Running that on all regions now. Command: `for host in $(cat canary-hosts); do curl -X POST https://$host/admin/refresh-jwks -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'; done`

Maria R.: rolling refresh applied to canary and us-east. Observability shows token error rate dropping, but edges still show a tail.

Jonah L.: logs from signing-service: `WARN: key-publisher failed to push key f3c9d to jwks-store: timeout` at 10:11:58Z. network flake between signing-service and jwks-store? Checking infra.

Priya S.: I'm escalating to infra-net (ping @maria infra contact) to see if there were any AWS VPC issues impacting internal control-plane traffic.

Alex G.: customer impact: some user sessions failing auth and showing 401s on web app and mobile oauth flows. early estimate ~0.7% of requests, but for login-heavy customers it's higher. Marking impact: partial outage for auth flows.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to Sev2 by Alex G. (auth tokens failing for subset of requests).

Maria R.: quick mitigation checklist being executed:
- [x] Force JWKS refresh on verifiers
- [x] Re-run key-publisher job manually (`/tools/key-publisher --once`)
- [ ] Confirm signing-service isn't rotating keys mid-publish (temporarily halt rotations)
- [ ] Verify KMS key availability for previous kid if we need to revert signing

Jonah L.: Ran `/tools/key-publisher --once` against jwks-store; publisher returned 200 and jwks-store now exposes both `e7a2f` and `f3c9d` until we expire old keys. Error rate drops to 0.3% after full refresh across regions.

Alex G.: good. hold rotations for 15m to ensure no additional mismatches. Also increasing logs for token validation to capture `kid` headers and source ip for next 10m.

Priya S.: Notifying CS about impacted customers. Drafting message for status page: "We are investigating intermittent authentication failures which may affect logins. Mitigation in progress."

Maria R.: Confirming no errors in KMS — key material accessible. Suspected root cause narrowed to race between key rotation and key-publisher service retry/backoff.

pagerduty: PD incident PD-Auth-TokenFailure acknowledged by Alex G. (primary). Current status: mitigated (partial) -> monitor.

Alex G.: Starting postmortem doc stub: https://docs.redwood.example/incidents/PD-Auth-TokenFailure-1795006789 — will update with timeline, root cause, and remediation.

Jonah L.: Action items:
- Disable automatic rotation for signing-service for next 24h (Alex)
- Improve key-publisher retry logic and add circuit-breaker (Infra/Eng-Infra)
- Add end-to-end integration test that simulates rotation and publisher latency (Eng-ML/Eng-Platform)
- Postmortem and customer comms (Priya/CS)

Alex G.: handing off monitoring/handoff to @Maria R. — I'm paged for the next 15m if it spikes again. If it's stable in 30m we can de-escalate.

oncall-rotation-bot: Next on-call in 28 minutes: Jonah L. (secondary).

Maria R.: I'll keep watch and close once we've had 60m of stable traffic and no regressions after rotation resume. Please add any symptoms you see to the postmortem doc.

Priya S.: customer update posted to status page and sent to priority CS contacts.

Alex G.: adding final note: avoid emergency key re-issuance except via the key-rotation-runbook; do not manually sign tokens with legacy keys.

incident-bot: Posting incident timeline anchors: 10:11Z rotation attempt -> 10:12Z publisher timeout -> 10:13Z PagerDuty page -> 10:20Z forced JWKS refresh -> 10:34Z full recovery to <0.5% errors.

Maria R.: closing notes: starting retro and will schedule a short architecture review to harden JWKS propagation. If anyone needs read access to logs or postmortem doc ping me. :white_check_mark:

Alex G.: thanks team. moving to monitoring-only; leaving thread open for 1h for handoff. :thumbsup:
